profile.address: The Users Way, Google Berkeley County Data Center, Berkeley County, SC (5)
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Berkeley County, South Carolina data center campus, mapped on The Users Way near Moncks Corner, one of several OSM-mapped buildings on this street. Google's own South Carolina locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own South Carolina data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the Berkeley County campus opened in 2007 as one of Google's first data centers built in the United States, that the company has invested more than $13 billion in South Carolina since then, and that it generated $7.2 billion in South Carolina economic activity in 2025. Google also cites a 225-megawatt renewable energy purchase agreement signed in 2023, and community programs including longleaf pine and Church Creek watershed restoration and a $1 million Hurricane Helene home-weatherization contribution.

The Berkeley County campus, together with a newer Dorchester County facility opened in 2024, forms Google's South Carolina Lowcountry data center footprint, though Google's own public materials describe the region in aggregate rather than naming individual Berkeley County buildings or per-building capacity figures.\n\nSouth Carolina's data center sales and use tax exemption, administered by the South Carolina Department of Commerce, applies to qualifying equipment and electricity purchases and has been credited by state officials with helping attract and retain large technology-sector investment in the Lowcountry region.

profile.capacity_note: Google does not publish a megawatt IT capacity figure for any individual Berkeley County building; the campus has grown continuously since 2007 across at least nine OSM-mapped structures tracked in this registry, but Google's own public materials describe the South Carolina footprint in aggregate rather than per-building.
profile.facility_note: Google has not published a building-specific name, street address, or square footage for this individual structure within its Berkeley County campus; this entry is one of the OSM-mapped buildings within that campus footprint, distinguished from its neighbors only by street (The Users Way, South Google Drive, North Google Drive, or Great Heron Trail) and coordinate.
profile.research_note: Reading written 2026-09-03 (Sonnet). Google's own datacenters.google/locations/south-carolina page (fetched fresh this session) confirms the campus opened in 2007 as one of Google's first US data centers, more than $13 billion invested in South Carolina since then, and a newer Dorchester County facility opened in 2024; it does not name individual Berkeley County buildings, addresses, or per-building square footage, so this entry does not assign address specifics or facility_codes beyond the OSM-derived street name and campus label. A Berkeley County Assessor parcel lookup at this coordinate would be the next step toward a building-specific fact.
profile.regional_context: Berkeley County, in South Carolina's Lowcountry near Moncks Corner, was the site of Google's first data center in the state, opened in 2007, and the company has since expanded to a second South Carolina county, Dorchester, with a facility opened in 2024. Santee Cooper and Berkeley Electric Cooperative are among the utilities serving the area. South Carolina offers a state sales and use tax exemption on qualifying data center equipment and electricity, administered by the South Carolina Department of Commerce, that state officials have credited with helping attract and retain large technology-sector investment including Google.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Berkeley County, Moncks Corner, South Carolina, one of its original long-running US sites. The operator does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or building-level specifications for individual facilities on its data center location pages, so this campus's IT load is not disclosed.

Google announced a $500 million expansion specific to Moncks Corner and a combined $3.3 billion expansion across its two South Carolina campuses in September 2024. These investment figures place the site among Google's material infrastructure bets but do not specify how much of the capital goes to power and cooling versus buildings, nor do they translate to current or target megawatts. The state context shows 14 mapped data center facilities across South Carolina, of which only four operators publish power capacity, totaling 6.6 MW of disclosed IT load statewide.

Without published megawatt figures for this campus, its rank among sites that matter to AI scaling cannot be read from power consumption. The scale of Google's capital commitment and the site's tenure suggest it is a significant part of Google's fleet, but the absence of disclosed capacity means this campus cannot be placed in the state or national infrastructure hierarchy by the metric that binds AI compute to the grid.
